arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Clement argued that speech proposing unlawful transactions is unprotected. He stated that falsely proposing such transactions is also unprotected.
Mr. Diaz argued that the law carries severe penalties. He claimed the statute is vague and overbroad on its face.
Justice Roberts asked about a movie reviewer describing a film. He questioned if such a review violates the law.
Justice Ginsburg asked about a film showing a twelve-year-old. She questioned if the actor is a young adult.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the limits of free speech. The government claims that describing child pornography is illegal. The defendant claims that describing it is protected expression. The Court must decide if the law is too broad.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 30, 2007.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants the Court to uphold the law. It seeks to criminalize describing child pornography.
The defendant wants the Court to strike down the law. It seeks to protect speech about illegal materials.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues that proposing an unlawful transaction is not protected speech. It claims that falsely proposing such a transaction is also unprotected.
The defendant argues that the law is unconstitutionally vague. It claims the statute captures protected speech about materials.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Stevens asked if describing a war crime film violates the statute. He questioned if a person describing such a film commits a crime.
Justice Souter asked about receiving unsolicited child pornography. He asked if reporting it to police violates the law.
